title: Seven HiFloat8 studies: four P publications, three synchronisation protocols
formula: out(B*MQ,128) bf16 = sum_n hif8(exp(s - m)) @ V / sum(exp(s - m)), s = Q K^T / sqrt(128) over uint8 HiFloat8 Q(B*MQ,128) and K/V(B*N,128); the seven variants compute the same function and differ only in how P reaches L1 and how the two sides synchronise
study_for: `main.py`'s `KERNELS` map with `CASES` is the comparison table: seven variants over one unscaled-HiFloat8 body, each running the same six geometries, so what differs between any two rows is only what the variant's name says. Under sim all forty-two agree with the independent oracle to max_abs_diff 0.0 — the seven really do compute the same numbers.

Four ways to get a HiFloat8 P tile into L1 in NZ, differing only in the softmax `@vf` pair passed to the shared body: `nz1` MULTI4 squeeze then a masked strided store at pitch 129; `nz2` the same store fed by a uint8 gather at indices 0,4,...,252; `nz3` squeeze plus an even-byte zero interleave, a LOWHALF predicate and a uint16 scatter (the M10-031 ABI correction, whose zero byte is built as uint8 and reinterpreted because C310 has no HiFloat8 scalar broadcast); `nz4` the four-key native HiFloat8 deinterleave into four 32-key slabs at pitch 33, through `_full_nz4_body`.

Three synchronisation shapes over ONE schedule, which is the rarer comparison: `nd_fused` uses end-pipe-only C/V mutexes; `nd_mutexse` passes `_pv_se()` / `_p_se()`, the same mutexes with their start pipes declared equal to their end pipes; `nd_splitevent` keeps the plain mutexes, keeps `auto_sync`, and adds `ev_qk` and `ev_pv`, two `SEvent(Pipe.M, Pipe.FIX)`, inside the cube side. Same numbers, three protocols.

The construction that makes those comparisons cheap: every body takes its mutexes as arguments (`_cv_normal()`, `_pv_normal()`, `_p_normal()` and their `_se` twins), and the NZ bodies take their softmax pair as arguments too, so a variant is a different call and not a forked body.
do_not_copy_when: You need a production schedule. These are studies and their purpose is comparison; nothing here is tuned to be the one you ship.
You want a ranking. The unit records what each variant does, not which one won, and it makes no speed claim.

Your P operand is not the 64-key-wide HiFloat8 tile these publications assume. The pitch-129 and pitch-33 carriers, the MULTI4 squeeze, and the uint16 scatter's even-data/even-predicate lane rule are properties of that layout, not of the softmax in front of them.
